title: Which button takes the lift from floor three down to negative one?
description: The lift starts above the ground and must go to a floor below it, crossing the ground floor on the way. The movement is the target floor take away the starting floor, and the number of floors travelled gives its size. Keeko's doubt is that the button is positive because the lift travels four floors.
teaching_notes: One idea: the button press shows both how many floors the lift travels and which way it goes. Watch for students who give only the distance and forget that a ride down needs a negative button.

source: If the Target Floor is −1 and Starting floor is +3, what but
video_script.why: The child finds a button press that crosses the ground floor and sees that its sign gives the direction.
video_script.substitution: Use the book's own floors: starting floor positive three and target floor negative one.
video_script.anchor: the lift in {{NAME_10}} going down from floor positive three to floor negative one
video_script.wrong_move: gives only the number of floors travelled and ignores that the ride goes down
video_script.payoff_line: The button press is negative four.

names.{{NAME_10}}: the building with floors above and below the ground

maths_rules: movement needed = target floor - starting floor = (-1) - (+3)
(+3) + ? = (-1): 3 floors down to 0, then 1 more down, so 4 floors down, ? = -4
slip: +4 takes the lift up to floor +7
video_script.design: The shaft is drawn from floor positive three to floor negative one with the ground floor marked, and one arrow going down.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; the lift shaft with the lift at floor +3 and floor -1 below the ground

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the lift shaft is drawn
marks.ask: floor -1 lights up and a button panel appears with a question mark

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the lift in {{NAME_10}}.
<bookmark mark='start'/>The lift is at floor positive three, above the ground.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>It has to reach floor negative one, below the ground. Which button should be pressed?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: the shaft with floors +3, +2, +1, 0, -1; the ground floor 0 marked; Starting floor + movement = Target floor

marks.cross: the ground floor, zero, is marked on the shaft
marks.rule: the line Starting floor + movement = Target floor is written

narration: <bookmark mark='cross'/>To go from a floor above the ground to one below it, the lift passes the ground floor.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>As before, the starting floor plus the movement gives the target floor.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the target floor is negative one, and the starting floor is positive three.

beats.on_screen: To find: the button press (movement needed)

marks.find: the words button press are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the button press, which is the movement needed.

beats.on_screen: Movement needed = target floor - starting floor

marks.rule: the rule target floor take away starting floor is written

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step one, the movement needed is the target floor take away the starting floor.

marks.vals: the two floors are put in: (-1) - (+3)

narration: <bookmark mark='vals'/>Step two, put in the floors. We write negative one take away positive three.

beats.on_screen: (+3) + ? = (-1); an arrow from floor +3 down past 0 to floor -1

marks.arrow: an arrow falls from floor +3 past the ground to floor -1

narration: <bookmark mark='miss'/>Step three, read it on the shaft, positive three plus a missing movement equals negative one.
<bookmark mark='arrow'/>The lift goes down three floors to the ground, and one more floor below it.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The button press is negative four.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Check it, positive three plus negative four lands on negative one.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: +4 crossed out; an arrow from floor +3 going up to floor +7, far from floor -1

marks.up: an arrow rises from floor +3 to floor +7
marks.fix: the button is struck out and a downward arrow appears

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the button is positive four, because the lift travels four floors.
<bookmark mark='up'/>But a positive button takes the lift up, to floor positive seven, far above the target.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The button must also tell the direction, and this ride goes down, so it is negative four.
